title: Cold Weather Could Predict an Increase in Heart Attacks Three Days in Advance - Nautilus
gist: A Public Health study of 114,000+ out-of-hospital heart attacks in Hungary (2018-2023) links cold weather and other meteorological variables to cardiac events, suggesting weather could predict heart-attack surges about three days ahead.

insights.claim: A study published in Public Health found that cold weather could predict an increase in heart attacks about three days in advance.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Weather-driven demand forecasting for hospitals, emergency services and cardiac care staffing.

insights.claim: Hungarian cardiac specialists analyzed more than 114,000 out-of-hospital heart attack cases in Hungary between November 2018 and December 2023 against temperature, wind speed, atmospheric pressure and other meteorological measures.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Large dataset makes weather-health models more credible for health-system planning and insurers.
